facts.label: F1
facts.exact_fact: [F1] [[def-probability-path-and-velocity-field]]: a conditional density path is normalized for the endpoint law almost everywhere, and its conditional velocity is defined by the conditional continuity equation.

facts.label: F2
facts.exact_fact: [F2] [[thm-conditional-flow-matching-gradient-identity]]: under finite loss, positive finite marginal density, local endpoint domination for the conditional continuity equation, and dominated parameter derivatives, the conditional and marginal squared-loss gradients agree.

facts.label: F3
facts.exact_fact: [F3] [[def-neural-ode]]: for a fixed parameter, the neural ODE is the initial-value problem $\dot z(t)=v(t,z(t);\theta)$ with the stated initial condition.

facts.label: F4
facts.exact_fact: [F4] [[thm-neural-ode-global-smooth-flow]]: a jointly smooth field on an open time interval containing $[0,1]$, with uniform state-Lipschitz and origin bounds on compact parameter sets, has a unique global flow on $[0,1]$, and its terminal map is jointly smooth in initial state and parameter.

facts.label: F5
facts.exact_fact: [F5] [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]: the squared Euclidean loss is $\|a-b\|_2^2=\langle a-b,a-b\rangle$.

facts.label: F6
facts.exact_fact: [F6] [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]: the expectation of a finite sum of integrable random vectors is the sum of their expectations, componentwise.

facts.label: F7
facts.exact_fact: [F7] [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]]: the law of a measurable map $S$ under $\mu_0$ assigns a Borel set $A$ the measure $\mu_0(S^{-1}(A))$.

facts.label: F8
facts.exact_fact: [F8] [[def-conditional-expectation-given-a-sigma-algebra]]: for an integrable real random variable, a conditional-expectation version is measurable, integrable, and has the same integrals on every event in the conditioning sigma-algebra; vector statements apply coordinatewise.

facts.label: F9
facts.exact_fact: [F9] [[thm-independent-random-elements-have-product-joint-law]]: independent random elements have the product of their marginal laws as their joint law.

facts.label: F10
facts.exact_fact: [F10] [[thm-change-of-variables-for-expectation]]: the expectation of an integrable function of a random element equals its integral against the law of that element.

facts.label: F11
facts.exact_fact: [F11] [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]: an integrable function on a sigma-finite product can be integrated in either order with equal results.

facts.label: F12
facts.exact_fact: [F12] [[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]]: the absolute value of an integrable scalar function's integral is bounded by the integral of its absolute value.

facts.label: F13
facts.exact_fact: [F13] [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]: a nonnegative product-measurable function has a measurable section-integral function and equal iterated and product integrals.

facts.label: F14
facts.exact_fact: [F14] [[cor-mean-value-theorem]]: a real function continuous on a closed interval and differentiable in its interior has each difference quotient equal to an interior derivative.

steps.claim: For the realized $\theta_N$ satisfying the exact-flow bounds, [F3] identifies the sampling equation as a neural ODE and [F4] gives its unique solution on the full interval and joint continuity of $(x,\theta)\mapsto\Phi^\theta_{1,0}(x)$. The terminal output is therefore measurable as a function of the independent initial draw and the training history. Conditional on $\mathcal F_N$, $\theta_N$ is fixed, so [F7] identifies the conditional output law by $\mu_0(\{x:\Phi^{\theta_N}_{1,0}(x)\in A\})$ for each Borel set $A$. This verifies that the exact-flow output is defined; it makes no claim that the learned field realizes the target path.
